angleRead.name: Simon Leary
angleRead.text: The Oaks are 8-1 and have won four straight, and the desk wants a long-view piece that treats that record as present structure, not as proof of anything beyond itself. I'm not going to write a recap or a celebration. I'm going to write about what a record actually is — a carried load, a sequence of small decisions that hold. The role change angle is there in the packet: someone's role shifted inside a sustained run, and the run kept going. That's the structural fact I can work with. I don't know why the change was made, and I won't pretend to. I'll stand outside the arena, metaphorically, and watch how a thing holds its shape when one hand lets go and another takes the weight. The piece open

plan.focus: A sustained record as a load-bearing structure, and what it means when a role changes inside it without the structure failing.
plan.why: The assignment is a long-view essay, not a game story. The record is the only solid ground I'm given. The role change is the tension. The piece should interpret that tension — continuity under adjustment — without inventing causes or outcomes.

plan.interpretation: A record is not a monument. It is a carried thing — a load that stays steady only because the hands underneath keep adjusting. When one hand shifts, the load doesn't fall; it just finds a new balance. That is the whole piece. The Oaks are 8-1. They have won four straight. Somewhere in that run, a role changed, and the run kept going. That is enough.
